note: Canonical CVE id of the proxy finding on 331 hosts; the baseline for primary-key lookup.
Lower-case CVE id (Sweet32, 8 hosts); probes case-insensitive extraction.
The only known-exploited CVE, typed with spaces for hyphens; it sits inside the 219-CVE kernel bundle, so the gold is that bundle's QID.
An ordinary CVE from inside the 219-CVE kernel bundle, written with en dashes as a PDF viewer pastes it; gold is the bundle's QID.
QID with a hyphen after the keyword (SSH Terrapin, 4 hosts).
Lower-case keyword and a colon; QID 38919 has no CVE at all and is the most widespread explained finding (341 hosts).

query: are we exposed to CVE-2024-6387 (regreSSHion)?
note: A CVE id embedded in a sentence; the words around it must not widen the answer beyond QID 42046.
An unexplained QID: it has no write-up, but its 45 hosts are resolvable from the detections, so its gold is itself.
Two identifiers of different kinds in one query; gold is the union of the named QID (RPC portmapper, 334 hosts) and the CVE's QID (TCP sequence approximation, 1 host).
The one CVE that the scanner maps to two QIDs (12 and 333 hosts); both are gold, and returning only one loses most of the hosts.

query: A regression in the remote-login daemon brings back an old bug in how it reacts when a connecting client fails to log in before the grace period runs out. The timeout alarm interrupts the daemon at an arbitrary point, and its handler calls logging routines that are not safe to call from such a context. A remote attacker needs no credentials: letting connection attempts time out is enough to trigger it.
note: From the diagnosis of QID 42046 and CVE-2024-6387, as a vendor advisory without product name or versions. Near misses: the other OpenSSH QIDs, above all 38919 (authentication bypass) and 38904 (remote code execution through a forwarded agent).

query: Do we have anything affected by the SSH server weakness where a hardware fault attack that alters one bit of memory can switch the 'login succeeded' flag on and let someone in without valid credentials? It is the one that covers every release through 9.6.
note: From the diagnosis of QID 38919, which has no CVE; a colleague's question. Near misses: 38915 and 38913, which share the 9.6 boundary, and the ten other OpenSSH QIDs, whose diagnoses differ only in the flaw and the version range.

query: The SSH client can be made to run attacker-chosen commands on the machine that starts the connection. When a configuration directive substitutes the login name or the target machine's name into a command line, special shell characters in that name are not neutralised. A hostile source-code project can deliver such a name through a nested sub-project. Fixed in 9.6.
note: From CVE-2023-51385, as an advisory. Near misses: 38901 and 105936 (the other OpenSSH command injection, in scp; see para-04), and 38919 and 38913, which share the 9.6 boundary.

query: heads up: the secure copy utility in our SSH suite runs shell commands hidden in backquotes inside the remote path, and the maintainers say they won't validate it. which hosts have it?
note: From CVE-2020-15778, as a chat message. Deliberately the one paraphrase with two gold QIDs: the scanner has two checks for this CVE (12 and 333 hosts). Near miss: 38915, the command injection in the ssh client (para-03).

query: Issue in the web server we run as a reverse proxy in front of internal apps: a client can list the forwarded-for style request headers in its Connection header, which tells an intermediary to consume them, and the proxy then leaves them out of the request it passes upstream. Backends that allow-list callers by source address can be bypassed this way. Releases up to and including 2.4.53 are affected.
note: From CVE-2022-31813. Near misses: 731830, the same header trick in a different product (para-08), and 731514 and 731521, which share the 2.4.53 boundary.

query: Request splitting in the web server's reverse-proxy module. A deployment is exposed when a rewrite or proxy-match rule captures part of the requested URL with a loose pattern and pastes the captured text into the address of the upstream request. An attacker can use this to get a second request past the front end, reach internal URLs that access controls should block, or poison a cache. All 2.4 releases up to 2.4.55 are affected.
note: From CVE-2023-25690, as a four-sentence advisory. Near misses: 731520 and 731521 (request smuggling in mod_proxy_ajp), 730403 (smuggling through an unclosed connection), 731613 (mod_rewrite and mod_proxy flaws fixed in 2.4.60) and 731513 (same 2.4.55 boundary).

query: web server HTTP/2 bug: a client keeps opening streams and cancelling them straight away, and the memory for the cancelled requests is only given back when the whole connection ends, so a patient client can make the process grow until it runs out of memory. which of our servers are still below 2.4.58?
note: From CVE-2023-45802, as a chat message. Near misses: 731514 (denial of service through an unbounded request body), 730403 and 731613 (crashes), and 731355, whose write-up also names 2.4.58.

query: Advisory for a Go-based, cloud-native reverse proxy. Before passing a request to the backend, the proxy stamps it with headers that record the host and port the client originally asked for, and backends trust those values. Over HTTP/1.1 a client can get some of these headers stripped, and in some cases altered, by declaring them per-hop in its Connection header. There is no workaround other than upgrading.
note: From CVE-2024-45410 and the diagnosis of QID 731830 (331 hosts), with the product described, not named. Near miss: 730529, the same header trick in Apache httpd (para-05).

query: Which endpoints still accept the old encryption algorithms with a 64-bit block size for TLS or SSH sessions? On a long-lived connection that carries enough data, repeated ciphertext blocks let an eavesdropper recover parts of the plaintext.
note: From CVE-2016-2183 and the diagnosis of QID 38657 (Sweet32), without the attack's name or the cipher names. Near miss: 38913, the other protocol-level cryptographic weakness in SSH.

query: which hosts are configured to pass packets from one network interface to another although they are not meant to act as gateways?
note: From the two-sentence diagnosis of QID 115284 (IP forwarding enabled, 333 hosts, no CVE), as a one-line question in other words. Near misses: 82054 (whose write-up mentions a gateway protocol) and 125001.

query: The command-line URL transfer tool and its library mishandle the certificate-status answers that a server attaches to the TLS handshake. When such an answer reports anything other than an outright revocation, for example that the responder was not authorised to answer, the client still accepts the server certificate as good. Only users who switch on status checking are affected.
note: From CVE-2024-8096, under one of two Ubuntu curl updates. Near misses: 200568, the other curl update (ASN.1 time parsing), and 200547 (certificate loading race in Python's ssl module).

query: Break-out from application isolation in Ubuntu's package manager for self-contained applications. When isolation is applied through the distribution's mandatory access control profiles, a package that has been granted access to the user's own files can still write into the user's personal directory for executables. That directory is put on the command search path by default when it exists, so a malicious package can plant scripts that the user later runs unrestricted.
note: From CVE-2024-1724 (snapd). Near misses: 6021318, the AppArmor update itself, and the two sibling snapd CVEs under the same QID, which are about extraction, not the search path.

query: On 64-bit kernels, a 32-bit program that asks to resize a file to a negative length is not refused. The legacy entry point of the file-resize system call treats the length as unsigned, so the file ends up between two and four gigabytes long instead of the call failing with an invalid-argument error. The regular 64-bit call and the path-based form of the call are not affected.
note: Kernel, 219-CVE bundle, system calls: from CVE-2024-42084 (ftruncate in compat mode). Probes retrieval among 434 near-identical kernel write-ups; siblings under 203845 resolve to the same hosts.

query: kernel fix for the built-in debugger console: auto-completing a function or variable name can overrun the input line when the cursor sits part-way along a line that is already full, because the length check looked at the wrong buffer's size. which of our Ubuntu boxes still need that update?
note: Kernel, 219-CVE bundle, debugger: from CVE-2024-39480 (kdb), as a chat message. Near miss in another QID: CVE-2024-35823 under 200519, an overlapping copy in the console's character buffer.

query: Information leak in one of the kernel's filesystem drivers. When a file handle is built without a parent directory, only ten bytes are filled in but twelve are handed out, because handle lengths are rounded up to a multiple of four. The last two bytes are whatever was in kernel memory, and they reach user space.
note: Kernel, 151-CVE bundle, filesystems: from CVE-2024-26973 (FAT nostale file handles). Near miss in another QID: CVE-2024-42076 under 203845, another leak of uninitialised kernel memory to user space.

query: When too many malformed frames reach a virtual tunnel network device, the kernel hex-dumps every one of them to the log. With a console attached, the virtualisation I/O worker thread spends so long printing that the watchdog reports a stuck CPU. The fix limits the rate of the dump.
note: Kernel, 151-CVE bundle, networking: from CVE-2024-27013 (tun). Near miss in another QID: CVE-2024-40904 under 203845, a lockup from excessive log messages in a USB driver.

query: The kernel's key retention service throws away the lifetime that user space sets on a newly created key and keeps the key for ever instead. Cached host-name lookups are stored as such keys, so they never age out and the host stops picking up address changes.
note: Kernel, 50-CVE bundle, key management: from CVE-2024-36031. Near misses in other QIDs: the key-handling fixes CVE-2024-42098 and CVE-2024-42229 under 203845.

query: Encrypted virtual machines on AMD processors: a virtual machine monitor that the guest does not trust can deliver interrupt vector 29 to the guest at any moment and so force the guest kernel's handler for it to run. Are any of our kernels old enough to be affected?
note: Kernel, 6-CVE bundle, x86 virtualisation: from CVE-2024-25742 (SEV-ES and SEV-SNP), one of the few kernel write-ups that is not a commit message. Near miss in another QID: CVE-2024-31076 under 203845, a fix for x86 interrupt vectors.

query: network card driver bug: a virtual function that the host hasn't marked as trusted can wipe the hardware address assigned to it from the host side, just by bringing its link down. do we have that kernel anywhere?
note: Kernel, 8-CVE bundle, network drivers: from CVE-2024-26830 (i40e), as a one-line chat message. Near misses in other QIDs: the unrelated i40e fixes CVE-2024-36020 under 200519 and CVE-2024-41047 under 203845.

query: A BPF program can corrupt the bookkeeping of the BPF ring buffer. By moving the read position forward before it asks for space, the program can obtain two reservations that share memory, and through the second one overwrite the hidden header in front of the first record. The kernel later trusts that header to locate the buffer and may crash. The fix rejects a reservation when the records still in flight would together cover more than the whole buffer.
note: Kernel, 8-CVE bundle, BPF: from CVE-2024-41009. Near misses in other QIDs: the BPF fixes under 200519, 200621 and 203845, and the tracing ring-buffer race CVE-2024-38601 under 203845.

query: OpenSSH 9.6 and below
note: Gold is every QID whose write-up names OpenSSH and states an affected range that lies entirely at or below 9.6: 11 of the 13 OpenSSH QIDs. Excluded because their range reaches above 9.6: 38955 (9.5 to 9.7) and 42046 (8.5p1 to before 9.8p1). 38913 is included on its CVE text, 'OpenSSH before 9.6'.

query: Apache httpd 2.4.53 and earlier
note: Gold is every Apache HTTP Server QID whose stated range ends at or below 2.4.53: 730403 (2.4 to 2.4.52), 730529, 731514 and 731521 (2.4.53 and earlier). The six QIDs whose range reaches 2.4.54 or later are excluded, although a 2.4.53 host triggers them too. All ten sit on one host, so only QID-level metrics separate them.

query: OpenSSH older than 8.9
note: Same rule as prod-01 with a lower cut: gold is the six OpenSSH QIDs whose stated range ends below 8.9 (prior to 7.6, to 8.3, through 8.3p1, 5.7-8.6, prior to 8.8, prior to 8.9). 38896 starts at 8.9; the other six reach past it.

query: Ubuntu security updates for the linux kernel
note: No version condition: gold is the six QIDs whose diagnosis is an Ubuntu security update for the linux package, which together hold every kernel CVE. Near misses: the 14 Ubuntu update QIDs for other packages, whose diagnoses differ only in the package name.

query: curl and libcurl
note: No version condition: gold is the two Ubuntu curl update QIDs, the only write-ups that mention curl or libcurl. Near misses: the other Ubuntu update QIDs on the same host.
Identifier negative (Log4Shell): a well-formed CVE id that the corpus lacks; the lookup must report it as unknown, not fall back to search.

query: Do we run MOVEit Transfer anywhere? Need to know if we are exposed to the SQL injection in its web application that lets an unauthenticated attacker read and change the database.
note: Free-text negative: neither MOVEit nor any SQL injection appears in the corpus.

query: Atlassian Confluence Server and Data Center: an OGNL injection flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code on the instance. All supported versions are affected until patched; block access from the internet as a workaround.
note: Free-text negative in advisory form: Confluence, Atlassian and OGNL do not appear in the corpus.

query: NetScaler ADC appliances set up as a VPN or authentication virtual server leak session tokens through a buffer over-read, which lets an attacker take over logged-in sessions without credentials.
note: Free-text negative (Citrix Bleed): Citrix, NetScaler and VPN do not appear in the corpus, though generic words such as 'buffer' and 'tokens' do.

query: Malicious code was found in the release tarballs of the xz compression utilities, versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1. Through liblzma, which some distributions link into sshd, the backdoor hooks RSA key verification and gives whoever holds a specific private key remote code execution before authentication.
note: The one hard negative: the vulnerable product (xz, liblzma) is absent from the corpus, but the text is about the OpenSSH server, the corpus's largest product family, so near neighbours such as 42046 and 38904 look plausible. Abstaining is right: no write-up covers this backdoor.
